content:
Apple continues to roll out beta versions of macOS 27 Golden Gate ahead of its official launch later this year, and has now released the fifth beta to developers. Here's what you can expect.

Apple releases macOS 27 beta 5

Three weeks ago, Apple released macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 4, followed by the corresponding public beta a few days later.

Now, the company is rolling out macOS Golden Gate beta 5, continuing to fix bugs and performance issues in preparation for the official release later this year.

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces an all-new Siri app, along with a redesigned Siri AI. It also includes a new AI-powered Shortcuts app that lets you build shortcuts with natural language prompts, as well as a prompt-based Safari extension builder.

In addition, macOS 27 Golden Gate adds new Golden Gate-themed wallpapers and screensavers, while also reverting the corner radius of windows and apps back to a fixed radius, reversing the change made in macOS 26, which adjusted the corner radius based on the contents of each window or app's menu bar.

The build number for macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 5 is 26A5406e. We're testing the new beta in detail and will report back with any new findings.

How to install macOS 27 Golden Gate beta

Here's how to install macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 5:

  • Back up your Mac
  • Open System Settings
  • Go to General → Software Update
  • Click the 'i' icon next to Beta Updates
  • Select 'macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta' from the dropdown menu in the top right
  • Click Done

Have you spotted anything new in today's macOS 27 Golden Gate beta? Let us know in the comments.
